articles.title: 'No excuse for venues not to use Ask for Angela'
articles.summary: Ten years after it began in Lincoln, the Ask for Angela campaign has become a charity.
articles.body:
The creator of the Ask for Angela campaign says its new charity status will help it support more people who feel unsafe on a night out.

Hayley Crawford started the scheme 10 years ago in Lincoln pubs and named it after Angela Phillips, a family friend who was killed by her husband in 2012.

Ask for Angela allows people who feel unsafe in bars or clubs to discreetly seek help. When someone "asks for Angela", staff can help them leave safely or take them to a secure area.

Crawford hopes its new status will encourage more bars to take it on. She said: "There's never any excuse why a venue doesn't implement Ask for Angela."

The Ask for Angela Foundation was registered as a charity in October and will be led by Crawford.

"Becoming a charity means Angela is protected for good, and I'm proud to lead it," she said.

"I thought the best way to protect Ask for Angela is to pull it into a charity and make sure it's there for people in the future and there's consistency, free resources, free training.

"It's just nice to know there is something in place to help people so they don't feel helpless or feel like they've got nowhere to turn."

Crawford started the scheme while she was strategic lead for tackling sexual violence at Lincolnshire County Council after seeing an increase in people experiencing sexual harassment through online dating.

Crawford said people had told her they felt safer after seeing an Ask for Angela poster in a venue and some had told her it had got them out of "really unsafe situations".

The scheme was originally trialled in Lincoln pubs, and was then taken up by police forces and councils across the UK.

It has since spread to Australia, where it is implemented in Sydney, Perth and Adelaide.

Failures were uncovered by the BBC in 2024 when secret filming found that in more than half of the London venues they visited, staff failed to respond to the code word.

In 2025, Phillips's daughter, Hollie, called for government action to ensure the scheme was implemented properly.

Hollie said: "Ask for Angela has given us such a sense of pride and closure, knowing that women who feel unsafe in public spaces are using her name for safety."

Crawford said the charity status would help solve the issue of pubs not implementing the scheme.

"Hopefully, that will give them the confidence to implement the scheme and not feel like it's going to cost them a lot of money, or it's complicated, or that they won't have the support in place because they'll be able to access that all through the charity," she said.

"I'd love every venue to have a poster in every toilet and every member of staff to know what to do."

Venues can download free posters, staff guidance and training on the Ask for Angela website.

articles.title: Panchkula school assault case: 8-year-old granted bail; parents barred from giving him mobile phone
articles.summary: Panchkula school assault case: JJB grants bail to 8-year-old after parents pledge no mobile access, counselling and supervision; video removal ordered in 15 days.
articles.body: PANCHKULA: The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB), Panchkula, has granted bail to the eight-year-old boy facing proceedings in the school assault case after his parents gave an undertaking that he would not be allowed access to a mobile phone and would undergo counselling, behavioural guidance and any treatment deemed necessary.The Class III student was represented before the board through his father.In the bail application, the parents undertook to take full responsibility for his care and supervision, while ensuring a healthy family environment, proper upbringing, education and moral guidance.They also assured the board that the child would undergo counselling, behavioural intervention and rehabilitation measures as advised by the competent authority.In addition, they undertook to provide him with appropriate medical care and all necessary support for his physical and mental well-being.The application stated that the child had cooperated with investigators and had no previous criminal record.It further argued that prolonged stay in custody could adversely affect his education, academic progress and overall development.The parents also assured the Board that they would ensure his presence whenever required and comply with all conditions imposed while granting bail.In a separate plea filed under Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, the boy’s father sought directions for the removal of videos, photographs and other content related to the case from social media platforms and public forums.The plea contended that such material could lead to the identification of the child and expose him to humiliation, discrimination and bullying.It also sought directions to the investigating officer and school authorities to prevent the further circulation of any material that could reveal the child’s identity.Acting on the application, the board directed authorities to ensure the removal of the assault video from social media within 15 days. The child had earlier been lodged in an observation home in Ambala.The board also directed that his studies should not be disrupted and ordered treatment after receiving a report from GMCH-32, which had recommended medical intervention after observing behavioural abnormalities.The matter is being pursued against the boy under Sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing simple hurt), 117(2) (voluntarily causing grievous hurt) and 127(2) (wrongful confinement) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. articles.title: Idaho voters focused on the real issues during midterms, like choosing the Winchester 1873 as their state gun
articles.summary: Idaho voters chose the Winchester Model 1873 as the official state gun, making it one of 11 U.S. states with an official firearm designation.
articles.body: Tuesday's midterm elections were a bit of a bloodbath for the Republican Party. If you're a conservative, chances are you are looking for any silver lining to cope with the fact that Democrats took the GOP behind the woodshed last night. I'm here to tell you it wasn't all bad, though, as states like Tennessee and Florida are still looking pretty red, so there's no need to get too down in the dumps. AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI One state that certainly has voters with their priorities straight is Idaho, and I'm not just saying that because their state GOP incumbents completed a clean sweep at the polls. It seems the voters all throughout The Gem State were focused on the real issues that have been at the top of everyone's mind. Not healthcare or grocery prices, but rather which firearm would become the official state gun of Idaho. No, I'm not kidding. Six different firearms were presented on the ballot, presenting quite a grab bag of options, from a Colt .45 to an M1 Garand. And the winner is... And what a winner we have! The Winchester Model 1873, aka "The Gun that Won the West," is now the official state gun of Idaho. Man, what a crushing blow for the "Peacemaker," I was sure he was going to pull away late. In all seriousness, that's a pretty cool thing to say. Some states have an official marine mammal or dessert, but Idaho has a state gun. CONSERVATIVES STUNNED BY 'CATASTROPHIC' MIDTERM BLUE TSUNAMI, BLAME TRUMP'S IRAN WAR, HIGH GAS PRICES It’s actually not uncommon, either, as 11 U.S. states now have an official firearm. Most of the states on the list are pretty predictable, including Texas and West Virginia. I was surprised to see Pennsylvania included, though, while my beloved Sunshine State is nowhere to be found. Regardless, whenever your conservative buddies get a little down in the dumps this week, just remind them that Idaho now has a state gun. articles.title: 1 killed, 2 others injured when helicopter crashes into bay near Miami, officials say
articles.summary: South Florida has experienced heavy showers over the past few days, but it wasn’t known whether the weather contributed to the crash.
articles.body: MIAMI — One man was killed and two others were critically injured Wednesday when their helicopter crashed into Biscayne Bay near Miami, officials said. The Robinson R44 II helicopter went down late Wednesday morning near Bill Baggs State Park, off Key Biscayne, while on a trip to record boats on the water, the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said. Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz said during an afternoon news conference that the two survivors were taken to a nearby trauma center in critical but stable condition. Rescue workers from several local agencies, as well as the Coast Guard and Customs and Border Protection, responded to the crash. When the sheriff's office marine patrol units reached the scene, they reported finding a good Samaritan trying to help one of the victims and take him to shore. Miami firefighters attempted to save his life, but he didn't survive, Cordero-Stutz said. Meanwhile, border protection officers found the two other men from the helicopter and turned them over to Miami-Dade rescue workers for transport to the hospital. Cordero-Stutz said the cause of the crash remains under investigation. South Florida has experienced heavy showers over the past few days, but it wasn't known if the weather contributed to the crash. Television news video of the crash shows the aircraft upside down underwater with two yellow floats attached to the bottom of its landing skids. Those emergency floats are designed to help keep a helicopter afloat in a water landing. Officials didn't immediately identify the helicopter's occupants. The sheriff said they were still working to notify family members. On Sunday, nine people died when a Learjet plummeted into the ground near West Palm Beach, Florida, with enough force to create a crater and pulverize the airplane. The National Transportation Safety Board is also investigating that crash.

articles.title: Mother and daughter die after suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada
articles.summary: Authorities in British Columbia say evidence suggests an animal may have been involved in the women's deaths.
articles.body:
A mother and daughter have died after a suspected grizzly bear attack in the Canadian province of British Columbia, their family has announced.

The women - identified as Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20 -were reported missing on 1 November when they did not return from what was supposed to be a short afternoon walk, the family said.

Their remains were found in a trail area in Bella Coola, according to the BC Conservation Officer Service (BCCOS), which said evidence at the scene "suggested an animal may have been involved".

Conservation officers are working to track down any bears involved.

Balcarras' remains were found on Monday and Reed's on Tuesday during search efforts by conservation officers and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP).

Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the BCCOS, said it was not yet clear if more than one was potentially involved in the women's deaths.

He added that any captured bear would be assessed and if it is found to have been involved in the attack "it will be dispatched in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety".

Balcarras and Reed were "two peas in a pod" who "got along really, really well" and shared many hobbies, Balcarras' brother, Josh Balcarras, told CBC.

"When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her," he said.

Balcarras had recently moved to Bella Coola to pursue a new career and begin a new chapter in her life, according to an online fundraiser to help the family with funeral costs.

Grizzly bears are listed as a species of "special concern" under federal legislation, and are an important part of the British Columbia landscape, according to Environmental Reporting BC .

Between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears are estimated to live in the province, according to the province's Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, which has classified them as vulnerable.

According to the ministry, conflicts between bears and humans are "relatively rare" unless the animals are startled or protecting their cubs and food.

But there have been a number of attacks in British Columbia in recent years.

A grizzly bear injured two hikers in the McGregor Mountain area in October 2025, one of whom died later due to critical injuries. The bear was later found dead.

The following month, a bear attacked a school group - also in the Bella Coola area - injuring 11 people.

The BC Wildlife Federation (BCWF) has said that reports of grizzly-human conflicts have risen since the province introduced a ban on hunting grizzly bears for sport in 2017.

"With no hunting pressure, grizzlies and humans will increasingly occupy the same spaces with inevitable consequences," the BCWF's executive director Jesse Zeman said at the time.

articles.title: Município presta contas ao MP das ações contra os impactos do El Niño | G1
articles.standfirst: O encontro contou com a presença do prefeito Carlos Augusto Balthazar, secretários de governo, representantes do Instituto Estadual.
articles.summary: O encontro contou com a presença do prefeito Carlos Augusto Balthazar, secretários de governo, representantes do Instituto Estadual.
articles.body:
O encontro contou com a presença do prefeito Carlos Augusto Balthazar, secretários de governo, representantes do Instituto Estadual — Foto: Divulgação

Rio das Ostras promoveu no auditório da sede administrativa, uma reunião com o Ministério Público, conduzida pelo Procurador-Geral, Renato Vasconcellos, para apresentar as ações que a Administração Municipal tem feito para combater os impactos climáticos extremos decorrentes do fenômeno El Niño. O encontro contou com a presença do prefeito Carlos Augusto Balthazar, secretários de governo, representantes do Instituto Estadual do Meio Ambiente (Inea) e da Concessionária Rio+ Saneamento e do representante do MP, o promotor de Justiça Lucas Fernandes Bernardes.

Durante o encontro, os secretários de Obras, Wayner Fajardo; de Meio Ambiente, Ricardo Torres; do presidente do Sistema, Autônomo de Água e Esgoto (Saae), Maycon Prata; e o subsecretário de Proteção e Defesa Civil, Edmilson Martins fizeram apresentações dos projetos que já estão sendo desenvolvidos no Município e os que estão previstos a médio e longo prazo.

Os representantes do Inea também explanaram sobre os serviços prestados pelo programa Limpa Rio, do Governo do Estado do Rio de Janeiro. Entre 2023 e 2026, a empresa já fez um trabalho importante de desassoreamento de 53 mil metros de corpos hídricos no Município.

Na opinião do promotor Lucas Bernardes, a reunião foi bem proveitosa porque as secretarias de Governo apresentaram as ações que já estão sendo desenvolvidas no Município. “O Ministério Público tem monitorado as questões estruturais relativas à drenagem de Rio das Ostras. Dessa forma, temos acompanhado o que tem sido desenvolvido para evitar alagamento e fiscalizar as providências adotadas para minimizar os impactos climáticos desse fenômeno. Estamos a disposição do Município para contribuir com a resolução desses problemas”, afirmou o promotor.

Ao final da reunião, o prefeito Carlos Augusto entregou ao promotor o Plano de Contingência da Defesa Civil de enfrentamento dos efeitos causados pelo fenômeno El Nino. “Agradeço a presença do promotor Lucas na reunião. Este é um momento único, tendo em vista que vários atores, do Poder Público e da iniciativa privada, estão unidos para debater sobre a atuação de cada setor para resolução de problemas. Foi uma reunião bem proveitosa”, declarou o prefeito.

articles.title: Ativista Joshua Wong é condenado a 10 anos de prisão em Hong Kong | G1
articles.standfirst: Pena é a segunda imposta ao líder pró-democracia sob lei de segurança nacional
articles.summary: Pena é a segunda imposta ao líder pró-democracia sob lei de segurança nacional
articles.body:
O líder estudantil adolescente de Hong Kong, Joshua Wong, à esquerda, está em frente a guarda-chuvas amarelos do lado de fora de um tribunal de magistrados em Hong Kong, em 2 de setembro de 2015. — Foto: Vincent Yu/AP

O proeminente ativista de Hong Kong Joshua Wong foi condenado nesta quinta-feira (5) a 10 anos de prisão por sua segunda condenação com base em uma lei de segurança nacional imposta por Pequim, em um caso que, segundo críticos, reflete a repressão ao movimento pró-democracia da cidade, que já foi bastante ativo.

Wong foi acusado em 2025 de conspiração para se aliar a forças estrangeiras com o objetivo de colocar em risco a segurança nacional, segundo a lei. Em setembro, ele se declarou culpado do crime, uma medida que normalmente pode reduzir a pena.

O ativista, de 30 anos, já cumpre uma pena de quatro anos e oito meses de prisão pelo maior caso de segurança nacional da cidade, relacionado a uma eleição primária não oficial, depois de ter se declarado culpado também naquele processo. Antes de ser processado pela acusação relacionada à conspiração, a expectativa era que Wong fosse libertado em janeiro de 2027.

O juiz William Tam afirmou durante a audiência de sentença que o crime cometido por Wong era de natureza grave e rejeitou a alegação de que seu papel havia sido limitado.

Ele também disse que considerou inicialmente uma pena de 13 anos de prisão, mas a reduziu devido à confissão de culpa de Wong.

Wong aparentava estar calmo e agradeceu a seus apoiadores antes de deixar o tribunal. Seus apoiadores acenaram para ele, e Tiffany Chin, ex-integrante do já extinto Scholarism, que já foi liderado por Wong, chorou.

O juiz afirmou que Wong poderá cumprir as duas penas de prisão simultaneamente. Restam apenas cerca de dois meses da pena referente à condenação anterior por segurança nacional.

A moradora ET Wong afirmou que, quando Joshua Wong era apenas adolescente, já tinha uma “visão ampla” que talvez nem alguns adultos tivessem. Segundo ela, ele percorreu um caminho difícil pelo futuro de Hong Kong, pelos direitos humanos e pelo movimento estudantil.

“Pelo menos para mim, ele não deveria ter passado um único dia preso injustamente”, afirmou.

Condenações de Wong são vistas como forma de desencorajar dissidência

Hong Kong já teve uma sociedade civil livre e dinâmica, marcada por intensos movimentos de protesto e por uma imprensa vibrante. Mas, depois que um movimento contra o governo abalou a cidade em 2019, as autoridades reduziram as opções dos eleitores nas eleições e prenderam muitos dos principais ativistas. Alguns veículos de imprensa conhecidos por reportagens críticas ao governo fecharam, e dezenas de organizações da sociedade civil foram dissolvidas.

Observadores afirmam que a condenação de Wong mostra a determinação das autoridades em manter ativistas de destaque presos pelo maior tempo possível, desestimulando ainda mais o ativismo da sociedade civil.

“As acusações com base na Lei de Segurança Nacional podem ser usadas repetidamente como arma para manter um determinado preso político na cadeia, caso o governo considere necessário”, afirmou Eric Lai, pesquisador do Centro de Direito Asiático da Universidade Georgetown, referindo-se à legislação.

Pequim, porém, considera Wong uma figura antichinesa que apoia a independência de Hong Kong, posição que ultrapassa uma linha vermelha para o governo chinês. As autoridades de Hong Kong também afirmam que a lei de segurança é fundamental para a estabilidade da cidade após os protestos de 2019 e sustentam que as ações das forças de segurança foram baseadas em evidências.

Acusação destaca atuação de Wong em lobby e defesa de causas

A acusação havia alegado anteriormente que Wong e o também ativista Nathan Law concordaram, por volta de 2016, em fazer lobby internacional para alcançar o objetivo de autodeterminação democrática. Segundo os promotores, antes da implementação da lei de segurança, os dois pediam sanções e outras medidas contra Hong Kong e a China. A acusação citou encontros de Wong com políticos americanos, como Nancy Pelosi e Marco Rubio, em 2016 e 2019.

Depois que a lei entrou em vigor, Law e outros ativistas avançaram nesse trabalho no exterior, reunindo-se com políticos estrangeiros e promovendo abaixo-assinados, segundo a acusação. Wong teria apoiado a iniciativa a partir de Hong Kong, utilizando veículos de comunicação estrangeiros e redes sociais para chamar a atenção de outros países e reforçar pedidos de sanções, bloqueios ou outras medidas hostis contra a China e Hong Kong.

O advogado de Wong, Derek Chan, havia pedido anteriormente ao tribunal que aplicasse uma pena que desse alguma esperança a seu cliente. Ele acrescentou que Wong deseja cuidar dos pais depois de ser libertado.

Amigos disseram que, durante os quase seis anos em que esteve preso, Wong continuou lendo livros e se exercitando, aprendeu sozinho a tocar violão e amadureceu sua forma de pensar.

Para seus apoiadores, Wong é uma estrela política que representa uma geração mais jovem, nascida nos últimos anos do domínio colonial britânico sobre Hong Kong, antes da devolução da cidade à China em 1997.

Apesar de estar atrás das grades, a influência de Wong aparentemente continuou sendo uma preocupação, pelo menos para o campo pró-Pequim.

Em setembro, uma reportagem de um jornal pró-Pequim criticou um documentário de 2017 sobre Wong disponível na Netflix por “embelezar” seus crimes. O departamento de segurança da cidade informou à imprensa local que o governo estava tomando providências sobre o caso.

O documentário, porém, chegou posteriormente ao topo do ranking de popularidade da Netflix em Hong Kong.

articles.title: 'Quando saímos, não existia mais aeroporto', diz paranaense que estava dentro de avião durante tornado em Chapecó | G1
articles.standfirst: Andrea Cristina Viganó, de Pato Branco, estava prestes a decolar com a mãe quando o fenômeno atingiu o aeroporto. Passageiros sentiram a aeronave balançar e foram avisados pelo piloto de que o vento a arrastava pela pista.
articles.summary: Andrea Cristina Viganó, de Pato Branco, estava prestes a decolar com a mãe quando o fenômeno atingiu o aeroporto.
articles.body:
A paranaense Andrea Cristina Viganó estava dentro de um avião prestes a decolar no Aeroporto de Chapecó , em Santa Catarina, quando um tornado atingiu a cidade na manhã desta quarta-feira (4). A aeronave chegou a ser arrastada pelo vento, segundo relato da passageira, e o voo foi cancelado. Quando conseguiu desembarcar, Andrea encontrou parte da estrutura do aeroporto destruída.

"Foi uma coisa muito estranha, porque nós entramos no avião e saímos de um aeroporto perfeito. [...] Dentro da tempestade, nós passamos uns dez minutos e, quando nós saímos disso, não existia mais aeroporto", contou.

A Defesa Civil de Santa Catarina confirmou a passagem de um tornado por Chapecó. O fenômeno arrancou estruturas do aeroporto, provocou a suspensão de voos e também causou estragos em outros pontos da cidade.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, uma estação meteorológica de Chapecó registrou rajadas de vento de 93 km/h. Os equipamentos do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) marcaram ventos de até 126 km/h.

Paranaense presenciou destruição em aeroporto — Foto: Andrea Viganó

Andrea é de Pato Branco , no sudoeste do Paraná, e estava acompanhada da mãe, Celis Mara Viganó. As duas trabalham juntas em uma escola de inglês e viajariam para Campinas , em São Paulo, onde participariam de uma convenção da rede.

A passageira contou que os funcionários do aeroporto haviam tentado acelerar o embarque por causa da previsão de tempestade. Apesar disso, a entrada dos passageiros na aeronave ocorreu normalmente.

O avião começou a se deslocar pela pista em direção ao local de decolagem, mas precisou parar quando a chuva ficou mais intensa.

"Começou a aumentar, aumentar, aumentar. Foi um momento até que eu comecei a gravar o vídeo, porque a gente sentia o avião mexendo, embora eu olhasse pela janela e soubesse que o avião estava parado. Era uma sensação muito estranha, porque o avião balançava muito, sabe? Era algo fora do normal", relatou.

Segundo Andrea, o comandante avisou aos passageiros que a aeronave estava parada, mas enfrentava ventos de 140 km/h. Em seguida, informou que o avião, de 77 toneladas, estava sendo arrastado pela força do vento.

"E aí, naquele momento, a gente realmente ficou bem apreensivo, porque nós não sabíamos, não dava para ver muita coisa do avião. Era só realmente a chuva, e sentia todo esse balanço", contou.

Aviões particulares ficaram destruídos — Foto: Andrea Viganó

Depois que o vento perdeu força, o comandante avisou que o avião precisaria retornar ao pátio e que o voo não poderia continuar. Ao chegar ao local de desembarque, Andrea e os demais passageiros permaneceram por mais de uma hora dentro do avião, aguardando uma escada para desembarcar.

"Ele falou que não havia nenhuma escada mais disponível para a gente descer do avião, porque todas as escadas estavam embaixo dos escombros. [...] E aí é que a gente começou a olhar para fora e realmente enxergar o que tinha acontecido, porque os barracões estavam no chão, o terminal de cargas não existia mais", relatou.

Quando finalmente conseguiram sair, encontraram estruturas destruídas, falta de energia elétrica e dificuldades para retirar as bagagens.

"Para todos os lados que você olhava, você via só destroços e nada daquilo fazia sentido para a gente, porque a gente não tinha entendido até então que era um tornado que tinha passado ali", disse.

A paranaense também encontrou o carro que havia deixado no estacionamento bastante danificado. Segundo ela, a cobertura do local foi arrancada pelo vento.

Carros foram danificados pela passagem do tornado — Foto: Andrea Viganó

Viagem cancelada e dificuldades para voltar para casa

Andrea e a mãe tinham viajado de Pato Branco até Chapecó para embarcar no voo com destino a Campinas. As duas participariam de uma convenção de uma rede de escolas de inglês e tinham retorno previsto para sábado.

Com o cancelamento do voo, elas não conseguiram seguir viagem.

Andrea recebeu a orientação de procurar hospedagem e solicitar posteriormente um possível reembolso à companhia aérea.

A intenção é retornar para casa nesta quinta-feira (5), utilizando o próprio carro, apesar dos danos causados pelo tornado.

"Eu acredito que nós vamos conseguir voltar mesmo com o meu carro, amanhã, mesmo sem retrovisor, mas vamos devagarinho", disse.

A Voe Xap, concessionária do Aeroporto de Chapecó, informa que as operações estão suspensas por tempo indeterminado em razão de uma forte tempestade que atingiu a cidade na manhã desta quarta-feira (4 de novembro).

Equipes técnicas da administradora estão no local realizando vistoria completa da infraestrutura e adotando as providências necessárias para que as operações sejam normalizadas com a maior brevidade possível.

A concessionária orienta aos passageiros que não se dirijam ao aeroporto neste momento e entrem em contato diretamente com as companhias aéreas para obter informações atualizadas sobre seus voos.

articles.title: Winchester Model 1873 vence votação para arma oficial de Idaho | G1
articles.standfirst: Modelo 1873 recebeu 31,1% dos votos em consulta popular, mas decisão final caberá ao Legislativo estadual
articles.summary: Eleitores de Idaho escolheram o Winchester Model 1873 em consulta popular, mas o Legislativo estadual ainda precisa aprovar a proposta.
articles.body:
Eleitores de Idaho, nos Estados Unidos , escolheram o rifle Winchester 1873 como sua arma oficial nas eleições legislativas da última terça-feira (3), por meio dos referendos estaduais. O modelo recebeu 31,1% dos votos, cerca de 164,4 mil , e ficou à frente de outras cinco armas. A escolha, porém, não é definitiva e ainda precisa ser analisada pelo Legislativo estadual.

Conhecido como "A arma que venceu o Oeste", o rifle foi produzido entre 1873 e 1916. Segundo o Serviço Nacional de Parques dos Estados Unidos, foram fabricadas 720.610 unidades. O rifle ganhou popularidade no período de expansão para o Oeste americano, e também foi tema do filme "The Gun That Won the West", de 1955.

➡️ A expansão para o Oeste americano foi um processo de ocupação de territórios a oeste dos Estados Unidos, intensificado no século 19. O movimento envolveu a migração de milhares de pessoas em busca de terras e oportunidades, além do avanço de ferrovias e cidades. Também provocou conflitos com povos indígenas, que foram expulsos de seus territórios.

Revólver Colt Single Action Army, com 15,26%

Rifle Remington Model 700 recebeu 12,45%

A consulta foi incluída na cédula eleitoral por meio de um projeto aprovado por unanimidade pelos parlamentares estaduais. A proposta foi apresentada como parte das comemorações dos 250 anos da independência dos Estados Unidos , celebrados em 2026. O texto destacou a relação histórica do país com as armas de fogo, incluindo o uso de rifles durante a Guerra de Independência.

A votação foi consultiva e não obriga os parlamentares a seguir a preferência dos eleitores. O Legislativo de Idaho deverá avaliar a proposta durante a sessão de 2027. Nenhuma das seis armas escolhidas para a consulta tem ligação direta com a história ou a fabricação no estado.

No Idaho tiveram que escolher qual seria a arma oficial do estado. — Foto: Reprodução/X

Idaho se juntaria a outros dez estados americanos que já adotaram uma arma oficial. Utah e Arizona foram os primeiros, em 2011. Utah escolheu a pistola Browning M1911, desenvolvida pelo inventor John Browning, nascido no estado. Arizona adotou o revólver Colt Single Action Army, também conhecido como Peacemaker.

Cerca de 70% dos eleitores que compareceram às urnas em Idaho também participaram da consulta sobre a arma oficial. O estado registrou participação de aproximadamente 69% dos eleitores registrados nas eleições de meio de mandato, segundo dados preliminares. O índice ainda pode mudar com a inclusão de votos registrados no próprio dia da eleição.

articles.summary: Além de Chapecó, Xanxerê também teve tornado nesta quarta (4).
articles.body:
Uma câmera de monitoramento flagrou o início do tornado em Chapecó , no Oeste de Santa Catarina , na manhã de quarta-feira (4). As imagens mostram o vento forte destelhando imóveis (assista acima) . A veracidade do vídeo foi confirmada pela Defesa Civil municipal.

O fenômeno ocorreu às 10h30, confirmou a Defesa Civil estadual após analisar dados do radar meteorológico. Poucos minutos depois, a vizinha Xanxerê registrou outro tornado.

Os dados mostraram circulação rotativa dos ventos no interior de tempestades intensas , o que reforça a confirmação do fenômeno. Uma estação do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) registrou rajadas de 126 km/h na cidade .

Início do tornado em Chapecó — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Outro tornado foi confirmado na mesma região

A Defesa Civil confirmou a passagem de um segundo tornado no estado nesta quarta-feira (4). O fenômeno foi registrado em Xanxerê às 10h48.

Os municípios ficam a cerca de 44 quilômetros de distância. Ambos estão na rota de uma linha de instabilidade que começou pelo Extremo-Oeste e avançou em direção ao Meio-Oeste, áreas que concentram a maioria das ocorrências.

🌪️ O tornado é caracterizado por uma coluna de ar em rotação que se estende da base de uma nuvem de tempestade até o solo, apresentando alto potencial destrutivo devido aos ventos intensos ( leia outros detalhes aqui )

Todo o estado esteve sob alerta vermelho do Inmet para temporais na quarta. As fortes chuvas provocaram a morte de um homem em Rio Negrinho , no Norte catarinense.

O Aeroporto de Chapecó também foi atingido e pousos e decolagens foram suspensos até sexta-feira. Parte da estrutura metálica da entrada do terminal foi arrancada pelo vento e vidraças foram quebradas.

Temporal arrancou estruturas e suspendeu atividades do Aeroporto de Chapecó — Foto: NSC TV/Reprodução

Temporal arranca estruturas e suspende atividades em Aeroporto de Chapecó; VÍDEO — Foto: Reprodução/NSC TV

A identificação do fenômeno ocorreu após a análise do radar meteorológico, que apontaram a presença de detritos levantados pela força dos ventos e uma assinatura de rotação associada à formação de um mesovórtice (rotação do vento) .

Segundo o órgão, a combinação desses elementos reforça a confirmação da ocorrência do tornado. Ao longo do dia, um drone irá sobevoar a região para detalhar os estragos.

articles.title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients
articles.summary: Is it symptom a health service at breaking point - or a positive way of involving the public?
articles.body:
Burns was able to put him at ease. She is part of a team running virtual clinics that support more than 100 patients and family members a week: "No matter what stage they are at, we try to help," she says. She explained the discharge process and where to go for help. The man's mother was soon back where she wanted to be.

Traditionally, a service like this would have been run by the National Health Service – but the clinic, which was set up during Covid and continued because of strong demand, is entirely funded by the charity Dementia UK.

The charity's chief nursing officer Paul Edwards says it is "trying to fill the gaps" within stretched NHS services. Burns adds: "The NHS and social care are under such huge pressure and dementia cases are rising - it's not always easy to get the support you need."

Dementia UK is just one of many charities working in the health sphere. From children's care to mental health and cancer services, charities are playing an increasingly important role in caring for patients.

Some - largely in England - have formal NHS contracts, while others work side-by-side with the health service across the UK, trying to provide additional support to patients in a way the NHS cannot.

A desire from governments of different parties from the 1990s onwards to develop a market of providers – NHS, private and voluntary sector – has meant the charity sector is now big business in health.

It's estimated that cancer charities alone raise more than £1bn a year, and the NHS in England spends nearly £2bn a year buying services from the not-for-profit and voluntary sector.

But there are concerns about the scale of charities' involvement in delivering frontline services - including from within the voluntary sector itself. Those directly providing services say they are having to subsidise squeezed NHS budgets.

And despite the good intentions of the charitable sector, some critics say its work with the NHS means more money ends up in wealthier communities. Defenders of charities' involvement, however, say much-needed funding should be welcomed.

So is the growing role of charities a symptom of a health service at breaking point - or a positive way of involving the public in their health care? And what are the risks?

There's nothing new about UK health charities taking on a major role in delivering services. Prior to 1948, British healthcare was provided through a patchwork of local charities, voluntary organisations, local authorities and private arrangements. Many hospitals depended on charitable donations, subscriptions and fundraising events to survive.

The creation of the NHS transformed this model. Most hospitals were brought into public ownership and funded through taxation. NHS founder Aneurin Bevan believed healthcare should not depend on charity, and restrictions were placed on NHS hospital charities actively raising money. But they did not disappear completely - they could still receive gifts and donations.

A major shift came with the Health Services Act 1980, which encouraged a more active fundraising culture. From then on, NHS charities expanded significantly and became increasingly professionalised. By the 1990s and beyond, they were raising substantial sums for equipment, buildings, research, and the likes of play areas in children's wards and well-equipped staff rooms.

Today, distinct from charities devoted to particular diseases or conditions, there are now more than 220 NHS charities attached to hospitals or community services, which raise £620m a year.

Ellie Orton, chief executive of NHS Charities Together, which represents them, says that while this sum may sound high, it represents only around 0.3% of the health budget.

She says the very purpose of the charities is to provide support, equipment and services that are additional to what the NHS provides. Recent schemes involve things like CPR training for members of the public, defibrillators being placed in community venues and green spaces in hospitals.

But it is a fine line. Scanners, blood transfusion equipment and emergency department co-ordinators have also been funded by charities. Some would say say core NHS functions like these are exactly what we pay our taxes for.

Orton defends this. "It's just the way it is now. We shouldn't get too ideological about this. It's not helpful to think the state can do everything. Yes we pay taxes but that has to cover lots – and it's finite. If our fund-raising means a parent of an ill child can stay close to their child while they are in hospital in a room funded by a charity, why not?"

And she says her discussions with the government suggest that there is increasing interest in what charities can raise and also what larger philanthropic donations by individuals or organisations can achieve.

In recent years, huge one-off sums have been raised. During the pandemic, the NHS Charities Together Covid appeal resulted in a £10m donation by the trading firm XTX Markets, while the Rausing family - best known for founding the food packaging giant Tetra Pak – gave £5m.

Rugby league legend Sir Kevin Sinfield's fundraising in support of his friend Rob Burrow helped bring in £6.8m for a specialist motor neurone disease centre at Leeds Teaching Hospitals.

"Of course, we are not talking about going back to a pre-1948 situation, but there is real interest in what such philanthropy can do," says Orton.

But there are inequalities. The NHS charity sector is dominated by some of the big London hospitals and specialist cancer and children's centres. The Royal Marsden and Great Ormond Street charities between them are responsible for nearly a sixth of the investment made by NHS charities.

"This does concern us," admits Orton. "It's not always a level playing field, but the answer to that is to help the NHS charities that don't raise as much to raise more."

The legislation change in the 1980s, coupled with the market reforms of the 1990s, also helped pave the way for specialist disease-specific charities such as Macmillan, Marie Curie and Dementia UK to get involved in the delivery of NHS services.

For example, over the past three decades, Dementia UK has developed a well-established network of specialist dementia nurses known as Admiral Nurses, who work in a range of hospital and community settings. The model is based on the charity co-funding posts with the NHS for up to two years with the expectation that the NHS will then take on the funding.

But with demand increasing, Edwards says it is becoming a "struggle" to get the funding needed from the NHS or from donations. "We are being asked to fund them for longer or find more than half the cost," he says. "Services are really being cut back."

And it is not just in dementia care that charities are noticing a squeeze. The charity WellChild has helped establish a network of 54 specialist nurses who work with very sick children. It funds these posts for the first three years, before responsibility for funding is expected to transfer to the NHS.

But disappointingly for the charity, for the first time this year a nurse post was not kept on, says Amy Mitchell, WellChild's director of programmes. What's more, WellChild's nurses are only meant to carry a caseloads of 15, but the average is currently 40. "Services are being dismantled - and our nurses are propping things up," Mitchell adds.

Others in the voluntary sector agree. Charities are increasingly being asked to do more with less, says Mark Yates, chief operating officer of Rethink Mental Illness, "and there is too often an expectation that we will absorb shortfalls ourselves to keep essential services running".

Parkinson's UK told the BBC its funding has helped the NHS pay for around 70% of the specialist nurses working in the field - and its chief executive officer Caroline Rassell says it's unfair on people affected by the disease.

"Charities having to fund these posts is effectively an additional 'tax' on people with Parkinson's as they are our main donors," says Rassell. "Nursing care should be the cornerstone of what the NHS offers."

Polling by the National Council for Voluntary Organisations shows 71% of health charities say the value of their contracts are not enough to meet the demand for the services they provide with many using their own donations to keep them going.

The survey dates back to 2023, but the NCVO says there is nothing to suggest the situation has eased.

NCVO chief influencing officer Leigh Brimicombe says it's quite clear charities are having to "subsidise" the NHS and wider public services and the government needs to address it by offering contracts that "cover the full cost of delivery".

"Otherwise, we run the risk of services being reduced or cut completely, at a time that communities in need are relying on them most."

For its part, the NHS is adamant that charities remain a valuable partner. NHS England points out that while the value of contracts to the voluntary sector in terms of proportion of the budget has dropped, it has still risen in cash terms.

In a statement, NHS England told the BBC the current 10-year plan looks to build on the "potential" of these partnerships and given the sector a "stronger voice" in health and care.

It's a complex relationship, believes Helen Gilburt, of the King's Fund think tank. Charities bring "real benefits" through their expertise and close ties to communities, she says, and there is "an element of subsidising" as the NHS seeks savings. But the situation has also "created inequalities" in the funding and support available for different diseases, she believes.

For instance, some areas, like cancer, have an established charitable sector "which is able to attract large amounts of funding", she says. These charities have been able to advocate for their patients, work with the NHS to enhance specialist services, and use their funds to develop services of their own.

Then, she says, there are charities in some sectors - "Parkinson's and dementia are good examples" – which are investing their own funds to develop specialist roles. "But they would argue this does not go far enough to meet the needs of people they serve.

"Then there are other areas, like sickle cell disease for example, where the charity sector is small and has even less funding."

Inequalities exist within sectors, too, say experts. Take hospices, for instance. "The fact remains that some communities will be able to give more than others, leading to inequalities in hospice provision," says Toby Porter, chief executive officer of Hospice UK.

And as a result, says Sarah Scobie, deputy director of research at the Nuffield Trust think tank, "more people from deprived areas die in the place where most people say they don't want to die – in hospital".

Not all of these differences can be explained by fundraising capacity. Health literacy – people's ability to navigate services and advocate for themselves – can also affect access to support, she says.

But her concern is clear – the scale of charity involvement in the NHS can widen inequalities.

As Orton points out, the UK is not returning to the pre-NHS era, when healthcare depended on charitable giving. Yet charities are no longer operating on the margins of the system, either.

articles.title: US-funded vaccine trial on babies cancelled in Guinea-Bissau after uproar
articles.summary: The trial was condemned as "unethical" and "neocolonial" because half of the babies would not be given the vaccine.
articles.body:
A proposed trial of a hepatitis B vaccine on newborn babies in Guinea-Bissau has been cancelled following accusations that the trial was "unethical" and "neocolonial".

The trial was funded by the US, under Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has a long record of expressing scepticism about vaccines.

Police have seized a batch of vaccines from the research centre at the heart of the controversy.

The proposed trial drew international criticism because it planned to withhold a vaccine recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) from half of the participating newborns.

Some public health experts argued that the proposed trial raised broader questions about whether vulnerable populations in African countries were being asked to take risks that researchers would not accept in wealthier countries.

The BBC has asked the US department of health and human services for comment.

The study was planned at the Bandim Health Project, a research centre that has operated in Guinea-Bissau since 1978.

It was designed to involve 14,000 newborns, with half receiving a hepatitis B vaccine shortly after birth and the other half not being given the shot .

Bandim said the trial aimed to investigate whether the hepatitis B vaccine given at birth has broader health effects beyond preventing infection.

Previous studies in The Gambia and Guinea-Bissau have raised questions about a possible link to increased mortality.

Researchers argued that because Guinea-Bissau does not currently offer routine hepatitis B vaccinations at birth, despite WHO recommendations, they have a unique opportunity to study its effects before such vaccines are introduced in 2028.

But critics questioned the ethics of withholding the vaccine from some babies, particularly in one of the world's poorest countries, where the infection is widespread.

The Trump administration funded the proposed study, with the CDC awarding the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) $1.6m (£1.2m) in December 2025 .

Walter Kazadi Mulombo, the WHO representative in Guinea-Bissau, told the BBC they became concerned after receiving questions about the study and finding no publicly available protocol.

He said the main ethical concern was that the trial would withhold an intervention already proven to protect newborns against hepatitis B.

"The vaccine has been used for more than 30 years in more than 115 countries," he said. "A study that will withhold that intervention from other newborns is unethical."

He warned that babies could be exposed to the virus during childbirth if their mothers were infected, as well as later in life.

Nearly a fifth of the population of Guinea-Bissau are infected with hepatitis B, a viral infection that affects the liver.

Those infected during infancy are particularly likely to develop chronic infections, which kill up to 25% of people, mostly through liver failure or liver cancer, according to data published in 2020.

The WHO is working with the government to bring forward the birth-dose vaccine.

"The country had been expected to add it to its routine immunisation schedule in 2028, but officials are considering introducing it in the first quarter of next year," Mulombo said.

Guinea-Bissau currently vaccinates children against hepatitis B at six weeks, which means it is less effective.

Guinea-Bissau's government prohibited hepatitis B vaccine trials involving children in January. At the time, it requested a team of experts from the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) to help evaluate the study.

Health Minister Quinhin Nantote said in October that the suspension remained in force and had not been overturned by the Council of Ministers after reports emerged claiming that the trial would be taking place after all.

"We were surprised to learn from media reports that the study might proceed," Nantote said. "We are outraged because even I, as the minister responsible for this sector, was not informed."

The dispute intensified after the SDU said a revised study protocol had received ethical approval "from the relevant authorities in Guinea-Bissau," which Nantote denied.

Dr Gavin Yamey, a professor of global health and public policy at Duke University in the US, criticised the proposal.

"The proposed trial reeks of neocolonialism," he told the BBC, questioning why the research was not being conducted in Denmark.

His criticism centred on the decision to withhold a recommended vaccine from some newborns in a country where hepatitis B is widespread.

SDU dean Jakob Grauslund said the trial had never started, no babies had been enrolled and no vaccinations administered as part of the research.

The SDU said it had received a separate, positive assessment from the university's own research ethics committee.

Grauslund said the university had sought an additional independent assessment, although Danish law did not require one.

He added that the relevant Danish statutory research ethics bodies were unable to undertake the review.

Following the approval from the SDU's ethics committee, Grauslund decided that the project could proceed.

He, however, stressed that this did not replace the separate authorisation required from Guinea-Bissau's authorities.

On 19 October, Guinea-Bissau's Judicial Police searched the Bandim Health Project's facilities in the capital, Bissau, and seized a batch of hepatitis B vaccines.

Police said the batch was intended for vaccinating children but did not disclose how many doses had been seized or the specific grounds for the investigation.

They stressed that the seizure did not, in itself, mean the vaccines were defective or unsafe.

The police have not explicitly said whether their investigation relates to the proposed trial, the importation of the vaccines or other circumstances surrounding the batch.

Grauslund said he could not comment on the seizure of the vaccines.

The proposed trial was funded by the US government at a time of significant changes to vaccine policy under President Donald Trump and Health Secretary Kennedy.

Under Kennedy's leadership, a US vaccine panel attempted to end a longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive a hepatitis B vaccine at birth, but a federal judge later blocked this, along with other changes to vaccine policy made by the Trump administration.

Critics have questioned whether the research could help support that policy shift, although the study's stated aim was to investigate potential effects of the vaccine beyond preventing infection.

Kennedy has praised the Danish researchers as "the deities of vaccine research", and cited earlier findings from their work in support of concerns about vaccine safety. A subsequent study by some of the same researchers, however, found no evidence of the previously reported effect.

There is no evidence in the information available that the proposed trial was designed to justify a change in US policy.

articles.title: DSA accused of ‘elevating’ antisemitic, pro-terror rhetoric after Hasan Piker hosts election stream
articles.summary: ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt accused the DSA of elevating antisemitism by choosing Hasan Piker to host its official election night livestream.
articles.body: The Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) chose controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker to host its official election night livestream, drawing a blunt response from Anti-Defamation League (ADL) CEO Jonathan Greenblatt, who accused the group of elevating rhetoric supportive of terrorism and antisemitism. "Of all the people the DSA could have chosen to host its official election night livestream, it chose Hasan Piker, someone who proudly expresses support for terrorist organizations and traffics in antisemitism," Greenblatt wrote in a post on X. "Let that sink in. The DSA isn't distancing itself from this kind of rhetoric. It's elevating it." The DSA saw several of its endorsed or supported candidates win on Tuesday night, including Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania, Melat Kiros in Colorado, Donavan McKinney in Michigan, Claire Valdez in New York and Darializa Avila Chevalier in New York. HASAN PIKER DECLARES 'WOKE IS BACK,' FANTASIZES ABOUT PUTTING DONALD TRUMP IN PRISON In his post, Greenblatt included a link to an ADL article with statements by Piker that the organization criticized, including comments the ADL said have "alluded to classic antisemitic tropes and conspiracy theories." The article contains some of Piker's more infamous remarks, such as when he referred to Orthodox Jews as "inbred" and his classification of Zionism as "an exterminationist ideology built around ethnoreligious supremacist values." Piker did not hold back in his response to Greenblatt, writing, "Suck it Jonathan, your best friend Elon burned 450 million to lose races all over the country tonight you bald piece of s---!!!" The ADL did not immediately respond to Piker’s remarks about Greenblatt. On Tuesday, Piker described the election as a "blue-clear apocalypse" after Democrats won major gains in the House and Senate. Pike livestreamed for more than 13 hours, offering his signature political commentary as votes were tallied. "Trumpism is dying, and I could not feel any better," Piker told his audience. "Just imagine a world where Donald Trump is in f---ing prison." He also gloated over Republicans' defeat, saying, "This is perhaps the worst possible scenario for the Republican Party. I think their odious agenda, their corruption, the destabilizing impact that they’ve had, the endless warfare and its consequences on the American economy, are finally coming back to bite them." RADICAL SOCIALIST WING'S HUGE NIGHT REVEALS ASCENDING CLOUT WITHIN DEMOCRATIC PARTY Ahead of the midterm elections, Piker drew attention in political circles as he interviewed and even campaigned with DSA-backed and DSA-aligned candidates. Piker came to national prominence after he campaigned with Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. While his race was not explicitly DSA-backed, the organization said El-Sayed "supports DSA priorities like Medicare-for-all." El-Sayed's decision to appear with Piker drew criticism. The candidate appeared to distance himself from the streamer, holding no additional campaign events with him toward the end of the election cycle. This came after critics accused Piker of suggesting that Jewish Americans' support for Israel could lead to antisemitic violence against them. DEMOCRATS CONDEMNING HASAN PIKER AS BACKLASH SPREADS THROUGH PARTY "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said during a Twitch stream in August. While El-Sayed did not outright condemn the comments, he responded to Piker, saying, "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past. "My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters. Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk." articles.title: Four dead, including Washington deputy, following domestic call shooting; another deputy on life support
articles.summary: A Spokane County sheriff's deputy died and another is on life support after a SWAT team was ambushed responding to a domestic violence call.
articles.body: A Washington state sheriff's deputy has died and another remains on life support after they were ambushed while responding to a domestic violence call that turned deadly, authorities said Wednesday. Spokane County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a home Tuesday after a woman ran to a neighbor's house reporting that her brother had shot her, FOX 13 Seattle reported. Responding officers learned the suspect had an active felony arrest warrant and had access to multiple guns and additional victims could be inside the home. NYPD OFFICER SHOT, GUNMAN KILLED AFTER ARMED BARRICADED STANDOFF IN BROOKLYN: POLICE The Spokane County Sheriff's Office deployed a SWAT team to assist at the home. As SWAT officers approached the house, a gunman opened fire from inside. "SWAT team members and deputies approached the house, attempted to breach the door and were met with gunfire," Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels said during a news conference. PHILADELPHIA POLICE OFFICER KILLED, PARTNER SHOT 12 TIMES IN AMBUSH; SUSPECT FOUND HIDING IN TREE Deputies returned fire and pulled the two wounded deputies to safety. Both deputies were rushed to a hospital along with the initial female victim who was treated for injuries that were not life-threatening. Inside the home, investigators found one person dead, while another body was found in the yard. The suspect was also found dead on the property. Authorities have not released the identities of those who died. PHILLY OFFICER MURDERED IN LINE OF DUTY PROMOTED TO SERGEANT AS POLICE FROM AROUND US ATTEND HIS FUNERAL On Wednesday, the sheriff's office confirmed that one of the wounded deputies succumbed to his injuries. He is survived by his wife and two children. "Although we know our deputies knew the risks, they bravely moved toward danger to protect others they did not know," the sheriff's office said in a statement. "They did this with honor and with an unwavering sense of duty to their oath to serve and protect the citizens of Spokane County; they heroically placed themselves in mortal danger." The second deputy remains on life support but is not expected to survive, according to officials. articles.title: West Hollywood unanimously passes ordinance granting protections for polyamorous relationships
articles.summary: West Hollywood, California's unanimous 5-0 vote granted hospital and jail visitation rights to people in polyamorous relationships through a city ordinance.
articles.body: West Hollywood, California, unanimously passed a city ordinance Monday that would allow citizens in "multipartner domestic relationships" to receive protections under city law. "It is hereby declared as the public policy of the City of West Hollywood that it is necessary to recognize and protect the right and opportunity of all persons to have multi-partner domestic relationships formally recognized and respected, and to be free from discrimination on account of their partnership in a multi-partner domestic relationship," the ordinance read. "Diverse relationship structures, including relationship structures involving more than two adults engaged in a loving, committed, and consensual relationship, are becoming increasingly common." PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH FACES INTERNAL REVOLT AFTER PROPOSING CLERGY MUST BE IN MONOGAMOUS RELATIONSHIPS The West Hollywood City Council voted 5-0 to allow people within a relationship involving three or more people to sign a statement with the city clerk. The declaration would grant qualifying partners certain rights, including hospital and jail visitation rights. However, the ordinance would not officially recognize polyamorous relationships as a "marriage" or a registered domestic partnership in violation of state or federal law. Still, West Hollywood is one of only a handful of local governments that have enacted some form of protection for multipartner relationships. Fox News Digital reached out to the City of West Hollywood's communications department for comment but did not immediately receive a response. POLYAMOROUS ‘THROUPLE’ FIRES BACK AT CRITICS OF THEIR RELATIONSHIP: ‘WE COME FROM DIFFERENT SCHOOLS OF THOUGHT’ In a comments to Fox News Digital, University of Virginia professor and Institute for Family Studies senior fellow Brad Wilcox lamented the passing of this ordinance for potentially normalizing polyamory and paving the way for polygamy. "The dangers of legally recognizing polyamorous relationships are twofold," he said. "First, it normalizes households where children live with adults who are not related to them by birth or adoption, an arrangement the research consistently links to higher risks for kids. "Second, it paves the way for polygamy, which the scholarly literature shows fuels gender inequality and hurts child well-being, because wives and children end up competing for a man’s attention and resources. "So, what seems like a progressive move here in West Hollywood can lead to some illiberal destinations that are bad for women and children." MASSACHUSETTS CITY RECOGNIZES POLYAMOROUS RELATIONSHIPS IN NEW DOMESTIC PARTNERSHIP ORDINANCE CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP West Hollywood first passed an anti-discrimination ordinance to protect polyamorous relationships in March. This latest ordinance will go into effect 30 days after it was adopted.

articles.title: New Jersey pre-K aide faces 61 charges, accused of filming himself sexually assaulting students at school
articles.summary: Shaun Stebbins, a former elementary school aide, faces dozens of charges after state prosecutors allege images and videos of students were found on his devices.
articles.body: A former New Jersey elementary school aide who worked with pre-K students for roughly four years is facing dozens of criminal charges, including aggravated sexual assault and manufacturing child sexual abuse material, after investigators discovered numerous images and videos of students on his electronic devices, prosecutors said. Shaun M. Stebbins, 44, worked at Woodbine Elementary School in Cape May County from February 2022 until his arrest in neighboring Atlantic County on March 29, according to the Cape May County Prosecutor's Office. The investigation expanded into Cape May County after authorities in Atlantic County and Somers Point notified prosecutors in April that a separate sexual assault investigation involving Stebbins at his home had uncovered suspected crimes in the neighboring county. FORMER NEW JERSEY MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER INDICTED ON NEW CHARGES, INCLUDING MANUFACTURING CHILD ABUSE MATERIAL A search of Stebbins' devices allegedly revealed numerous images and videos of Woodbine Elementary School students, prosecutors said. Authorities did not disclose how many students were involved or provide details about when the material was recorded. According to court documents, Stebbins filmed and performed sex acts on children in a school bathroom and during nap time, ABC7 reported. Cape May County prosecutors announced 61 charges against Stebbins on Oct. 30, including 29 counts of manufacturing child pornography, five counts of aggravated sexual assault, 13 counts of sexual assault by sexual contact and 14 counts of endangering the welfare of a child. The manufacturing and aggravated sexual assault charges are first-degree offenses that can carry prison sentences of 10 to 20 years under New Jersey law. The remaining charges are second-degree offenses, typically punishable by five to 10 years in prison. SCHOOL EMPLOYEE ACCUSED OF SECRETLY FILMING 12 GIRLS IN CHANGING ROOM FACES NEW CHARGES Cape May County Prosecutor Jeffrey H. Sutherland said his office continues to investigate the case. "Children are among our most vulnerable population, and we have a responsibility to protect their safety and well-being. Anyone who harms a child will be held accountable through our justice system." Stebbins remains in the Atlantic County Correctional Facility pending court proceedings. The Woodbine School District, the Cape May County Prosecutor's Office and the Atlantic County Prosecutor's Office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. articles.title: Israel’s Herzog accepts vote results, opens talks on forming a government
articles.summary: Move deals blow to Netanyahu’s efforts to discredit the elections, in which he and his allies lost their majority.
articles.body:
Israel’s President Isaac Herzog has accepted the certified results of last week’s parliamentary elections and begun consultations with party leaders on whom to task with forming the next government.

The moves on Wednesday dealt a blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s efforts to discredit the vote, in which he and his allies lost their majority in the 120-member parliament, while Arab-led parties made historic gains.

“The elections are over. Now is the time to face reality,” Herzog said.

In the October 27 vote, neither Netanyahu’s coalition nor the bloc of his chief rival, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, secured the 61 seats required to govern. The prime minister’s coalition won 53, while Eisonkot’s got 48.

That leaves open the possibility of an alliance between the two men or an alliance between Eisenkot and the Arab-led parties – Ra’am and the Joint List – which had secured a record 19 seats.

Herzog concluded the first day of consultations with party leaders on Wednesday night, and said talks would continue on Thursday.

On Wednesday, the president said he met with representatives of the Religious Zionism and Zehut, Shas, and Yisrael Beytenu factions. He “received their recommendations regarding the identity of the Knesset member upon whom the task of forming the government should be assigned,” Herzog said on X.

Three factions aligned with Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist base recommended that the prime minister be given a chance to form a coalition, while a fourth, led by a former Netanyahu ally turned rival, backed Eisenkot.

Eight more parties, including the two Arab-led factions, are scheduled to meet with the president on Thursday, with Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Netanyahu’s Likud going last.

Eisenkot’s prospects improved when Ra’am, a major Arab-led party, said it would recommend him. That brought his expected support to 56 lawmakers, according to the Israeli news site Ynet, which is still short of a majority.

The other Arab-led party, the Joint List, has not announced its position. Israel’s Channel 12 reported that the party was expected to coordinate with Eisenkot, endorsing him if asked or abstaining if he preferred. Its 11 seats could push him past 61.

Netanyahu’s 53-seat bloc, by contrast, may not yield 53 endorsements.

Degel HaTorah, which holds four of United Torah Judaism’s seven seats, said it would recommend neither candidate. The ultra-Orthodox faction broke with Netanyahu over his coalition’s failure to pass legislation exempting Haredi men from military service, The Times of Israel reported.

Once the consultations end, Herzog will choose the candidate he considers best placed to assemble a coalition, almost certainly Netanyahu or Eisenkot. He has several days to announce his decision, after which the nominee will have 28 days to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension.

If neither man succeeds, Israel would hold another election early next year.

Netanyahu and his supporters meanwhile have repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims that the Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, possibly with foreign assistance.

But Israel’s elections commission said earlier on Wednesday that it had conducted a thorough investigation of all parties’ claims of fraud and found “no evidence of irregularities that compromised the integrity of the election or affected its results”.

Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara also rejected a request to question elected officials without supporting evidence.

Herzog urged both camps to compromise to avoid a new election, saying they must accept that “not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled”.

“In the current reality, in which there is no clear winner after the elections, I ask for originality and creativity, courage and goodwill, so that the State of Israel emerges the winner,” he said.

He also backed investigating the suspected interference but warned against smearing Palestinian-Israeli voters, saying he had “great respect” for Israel’s Palestinian minority, which makes up about 20 percent of the population.

“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently,” he said.

articles.title: Election deniers lose races for governor in key US swing states
articles.summary: State leaders can hold significant sway over election administration, with implications for the 2028 presidential race.
articles.body:
After Democrats’ stunning blowout in the United States midterm elections , five Republican election deniers have come up short in their races to become governor in top battleground states.

Congressman Andy Biggs in Arizona, Congressman John James in Michigan, State Treasurer Stacy Garrity in Pennsylvania and Congressman Tom Tiffany in Wisconsin all lost their gubernatorial races on Tuesday.

So too did billionaire Rick Jackson of Georgia, a state that was central to President Donald Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential results.

All five candidates had either cast doubt on or voted to block Joe Biden’s victory over Trump in the 2020 election.

Jackson, for instance, had called Biden’s win “totally ridiculous” and criticised Georgia state officials for not complying with Trump’s demands to “find” extra votes.

“Our people really let us down,” Jackson said when he was pressed on the 2020 election during a campaign event earlier this year.

In January 2021, Biggs and Tiffany voted to overturn the 2020 results as members of the US House of Representatives.

Both lawmakers also signed on to a lawsuit that sought to invalidate results in Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, all states that Biden won in that year’s contentious presidential race.

James was not in Congress when it came time to certify the 2020 election results. He had unsuccessfully run for the US Senate during that election cycle. He later made a successful bid for the House of Representatives in the 2022 midterms.

That year, he acknowledged Biden’s victory. But he reversed his position in June, when he told podcaster Benny Johnson that the 2020 election was “rigged and manipulated”.

Garrity, who was elected to her current position in 2020, was among the right-wing politicians to campaign with Trump to reverse his election defeat.

She appeared at a rally in Pennsylvania on January 5, 2021, to call on state lawmakers to decertify the 2020 results. A day later, Trump supporters would storm the US Capitol, echoing the Republican leader’s claims of voter fraud.

Tiffany, Garrity and Jackson have since released statements or clarified their previous actions regarding the 2020 election and acknowledged that Biden won. Biggs and James, however, have not.

Al Jazeera has reached out to both of their offices for comment but has not yet heard back.

Tuesday’s midterm results are likely to have significant implications for the next presidential race in 2028.

Trump is entering the final two years of his lame-duck second term, and under the US Constitution, he is ineligible for re-election. It is unclear who will succeed him as the Republican standard-bearer.

Battleground states like Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin have all vacillated between presidential nominees of both parties in recent elections.

They will play critical roles in 2028, as the US looks to determine its next leader.

In some US states, governors play a major role in issues like voting access, election administration and efforts to redraw congressional maps.

Over the past year and a half, Trump has sought to rally state leaders to redesign congressional maps to help Republicans get elected.

Some Democratic-led states, notably California, under Governor Gavin Newsom, have responded with their own efforts at gerrymandering.

But it is unclear whether the push for redistricting will retain its momentum after Tuesday’s midterm results.

Already, Georgia’s Governor Brian Kemp, a Republican who was prevented by term limits from running in this midterm cycle, said on Wednesday that he would not call a special session of the state’s legislature to redraw the state’s congressional maps before his Democratic successor, Keisha Lance Bottoms, is sworn in.

Trump, after years of casting doubt on US elections, told The New York Times on Tuesday night that he was “absolutely willing” to accept the midterm results.

He also pledged to engage with the Democratic Party, which handily retook control of both chambers of the US Congress.

“We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” Trump said of the Democrats. “We’ll probably work something out.”

articles.title: El Salvador’s Bukele touts military intervention in Haiti
articles.summary: Haitian police have found a vehicle used by four missing Salvadoran technicians as Salvadoran troops deploy to Haiti.
articles.body:
El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele has posted videos of heavily armed soldiers from his country patrolling streets in Haiti and being greeted by locals.

“Gather your gangs so we can go fight with them,” Bukele wrote in a post on X on Wednesday.

The posts come as Haitian authorities say they have found the vehicle used by four Salvadoran aviation technicians who were attacked by gangs more than two weeks ago, but have yet to find the men themselves.

The country’s national police posted photos of the burned remains of a truck it said was used by the group, found in the Santo neighbourhood in the Croix-des-Bouquets community outside the capital of Port-au-Prince on Tuesday. The area, like much of the capital, has been under the control of gangs, which authorities are struggling to wrest control from.

Police were conducting a joint operation along with the United Nations-backed multinational Gang Suppression Force (GSF) and Salvadoran troops when they found the vehicles.

The disappearance of the four men on October 18 prompted the right-wing leader of El Salvador to dispatch more than 2,000 troops along with military hardware to the Caribbean nation.

Since being elected to office in 2019, Bukele has instituted a harsh crackdown on crime in El Salvador, jailing tens of thousands of people and imposing a state of emergency that rights groups say has suspended many civil rights.

On Tuesday, Bukele posted a video he said showed Salvadoran military helicopters opening fire on gangs attacking GSF soldiers from Chad.

“The gangs no longer have the upper hand,” he wrote.

In another post, Bukele said Salvadoran forces were there to help Haitians free themselves from the gangs. “We are right there beside you,” he wrote.

The presence of the troops has raised concerns among some about who is responsible for the use of force in the country.

Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for the office of the UN Secretary-General, told reporters in New York this week that only about 200 of the Salvadoran soldiers fell under the GSF’s jurisdiction.

“What is important is that any security operation be done within the framework of international human rights law, of international law, and that people’s rights need to be respected as you conduct security operations,” Dujarric said.

Haiti’s Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime, though, has assured the public the foreign forces are operating under Haitian authority.

“The international forces did not come to replace the state. They came to support it, to reinforce our capacity,” he said on Tuesday, speaking alongside the Salvadoran commander in charge of the country’s troops as well as Haitian and GSF commanders.

The leader of one gang, the 400 Mawozo, told the Associated Press news agency that he had written to the UN Secretary-General asking for an opportunity for dialogue. Wilson Joseph, best known as Lanmo Sanjou, said he was concerned about the killing of civilians given the surge in fighting.

Haiti has been without an elected government since 2021, when its last elected president, Jovenel Moise, was assassinated . Since then, successive transitional governments have tried to impose enough order to hold fresh elections.

Last month, the country’s nine-member Provisional Electoral Council announced it would delay national elections, pushing the first round of voting from December 13 to July 18, 2027. A second round of voting is also scheduled for October 4, 2027.

Authorities have pushed to register voters, with fewer than one million registered so far, out of some 6.5 million Haitians who hold identification cards that would make them eligible. Roads controlled by gangs have made it difficult for officials to reach registration centres, and violence has forced many Haitians from their homes.

The violence has also interrupted the delivery of food and other aid, leaving some 5.94 million Haitians facing acute hunger, according to an international food security assessment released last month.

Last week, Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said an uptick in fighting since the disappearance of the Salvadorans was having an impact on civilians in Port-au-Prince.

The group said 30 people, including women and children, had been injured in the eight days following the disappearance on October 18, by heavy gunfire and drone explosions.

The ongoing fighting had blocked civilians’ access to roads and bridges, and made travel to healthcare facilities “extremely risky” for people wounded in the conflict. The addition of international forces, the group said, was expected to make the situation worse.

“We fear that this armed conflict will claim even more victims, and displace even more people in the coming days, particularly with the arrival of additional international security forces,” Davina Hayles, MSF head of mission in Haiti, said in a statement .

articles.title: Charlamagne Tha God warns Democrats 'don't get comfortable' after winning House and Senate
articles.summary: Charlamagne Tha God demanded Democrats deliver on housing costs, healthcare, wages and corruption investigations after winning the House and Senate.
articles.body: Radio host Charlamagne Tha God warned Democrats not to let their midterm success go to their heads, warning they need to take action to show they are committed to serving their voters. That's why y'all won. I have one question. OK? What the F are you going to do with the power that we the people just gave you, Democrats? OK?" WHOOPI GOLDBERG WARNS DEMOCRATS TO 'TAKE CARE OF BUSINESS' AFTER MIDTERM WINS Charlamagne then demanded Democrats address a number of issues when they take office. What about healthcare? Are you going to fight to lower premiums, protect Medicaid? Are you going to stop Americans from going broke because they got sick? What about wages?" he asked. "People are working two and three jobs and still can't afford to live. What are you going to do to make sure a full-time job can actually support a family?" Charlamagne continued. "And while we're at it, what about all this corruption we've seen? And are we going to get real investigations into conflicts of interest? Huh? Government contracts and politicians using public office to enrich themselves? I hope so." "Once again, Charlamagne shows how clueless he is," Wold said. Charlamagne also credited Democrats for shifting away from culture war messaging and focusing on voters' economic concerns. "Ain't no talk of wokeness," he said. "There's no talk [of] identity politics. They're out there talking about affordability. And you got some really great quality candidates on the Democratic side.
